newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian rescuers spot two yachts, one survivor.
newsitem.headline: Australian rescuers spot two yachts, one survivor.

text.p: Australian rescue services searching for two solo round-the-world yachtsmen on Monday found two capsized boats but only one survivor in the freezing Southern Ocean between Australia and Antarctica.

The yachts and survivor were spotted shortly after one p.m. (0500 GMT), about 1,400 nautical miles (2,600 kms) south-west of Perth, Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Grasy told Reuters.
Briton Tony Bullimore, 56, on board Global Exide Challenger, and 29-year-old Frenchman Thierry Dubois on board Amnesty International sent out distress calls late on Sunday after running into a storm.

Gray said earlier on Monday that the yachtsmen were "in an extreme life-threatening situation".

The search plane had enough fuel to stay in the area for about two more hours before returning to Perth. A second plane had already been despatched and should arrive shortly after the first left the area.

The two competitors in the Vendee Globe race ran into difficulties about 120 nautical miles (220 kms) south of the region where French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli was rescued from his sinking yacht two days after Christmas.
Seas on Monday were rough with a six-metre (20-foot) swell and winds of 35-40 knots.
Gray said it was the longest rescue Australian maritime authorities had attempted for yachtsmen.
Dinelli was picked up on December 27 from his half-submerged yacht Algimouss after a search aircraft dropped him a life raft and helped guide a fellow competitor to his position.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a large-scale rescue mission to save French yachtswoman Isabelle Autissier.
